subject: history_social
passage: The corroded lump of bronze that sponge divers pulled from a shipwreck off the Greek island of Antikythera in ______ to be the remains of a geared device more than 2,000 years old. Working from X-ray scans of its fragments, researchers have shown that its dozens of interlocking bronze gears modeled the movements of the sun and moon, predicted eclipses, and tracked the four-year cycle of the ancient Greek games. Nothing of comparable complexity is known to have been built again for more than a thousand years.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject of the sentence is the long phrase "The corroded lump of bronze that sponge divers pulled from a shipwreck … in 1901," and its verb is "turned out." No punctuation should come between a subject and its verb, however long the subject is.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon must have an independent clause on both sides; "turned out to be the remains …" is not one.
explanation.B: Correct. The verb "turned out" follows its subject directly, with no punctuation between them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A single comma can't separate a subject from its verb.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A single dash can't separate a subject from its verb; dashes set off extra information in pairs or introduce an afterthought.
